Dewani week 4 of the trial

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Show:

Summary:
Week 4 of the Dewani Trial. Bondage Master Leopold Leisser took the stand briefly before his evidence was ruled inadmissible by Judge Traverso. Next up was taxi driver Zola Tongo sentenced for 18 years for the role he played in the murder of Anni Dewani. Despite Advocate Van Zyl systematically pulling Tongo's evidence in chief apart he stuck to his story that Shrien Dewani paid to have his wife killed.

Press Release:


Honeymoon Murder Week 4
Two key witnesses on the stand– male escort Leopold Leisser, also known as the “German Master” and Zola Tongo, the taxi driver Shrien Dewani supposedly hired to help orchestrate the murder of his wife, Anni. Carte Blanche unpacks new evidence from week 4 of the Honeymoon Murder trial.


Script:


Script: Week 4 of the trial was an intense one for Shrien Dewani.It was the first time in four years he had locked eyes with the German Escort Leopold Leisser who’s confessions of brutal sadomasochist sex which Dewani initially denied shocked the world. Even more damning was the evidence of taxi driver Zola Tongo

Link 2 Day 9 There was much anticipation ahead of the evidence of German bondage master Leopold Leisser but only early on there was an objection from the Defence about what he was going to tell the court as a as a result he was asked to stand down so that both sides could present written representation to the judge about the admissibility of the evidence

Script: Defence lawyer William Booth is following the case closely

John "Do you think it was a major shortcoming on the part of the state that they didn’t appear to be prepared for that objection?

William " I think the State has to expect that the Defence will object to aspects like this and they should have been completely and utterly prepared to deal with this and also take into consideration that the Judge might possibly rule against them

Script: Judge Traverso’s ruling came as no surprise to Times journalist Ruth Maclean

Ruth Maclean "I think Judge Traverso doesn’t want to entertain any kind of talk of Dewani’s sexuality that was made clear in the emails that she prevented the court from reading

Script: The Prosecution team presented lengthy legal arguments on the morning of Day 10 of the trial as to why Leopold Leisser’s evidence provided a context and motive for Shrien Dewani to get rid of his wife

QUOTE JUDGE TRAVERSO “ How long was the relationship between Mr Leisser and the accused, over what period did it stretch? “

Quote MR MOPP: M.Lady from September 2009, the last physical meeting was on 17th April 2010 but they were also in contact with one another subsequent to that, they were in contact in June, there was contact in August, they were in contact via Gaydar, … on the 3rd and 4th December 2010. So the period of contact is not only prior to the accused getting engaged and marrying the deceased, it spans an entire period.

Script: The State also wanted to show Dewani was gay and not bisexual, but Judge Traverso was not convinced, saying how he described himself on a dating website had no relevance in a surprising moment of levity

Quote Judge Traverso” If I describe myself as a beautiful young 24 year old it’s not going to help me is it?”

Script: Leisser was not the anticipated domineering bondage master. He spoke softly and merely confirmed the contact he had with Shrien, without going into any details.

William “Character evidence is not usually admissible in a criminal trial ……motive is not an element of the crime of murder but the state often does present it and will argue to counter any argument from the Defence as to why would Dewani would have got other people to go and kill his wife and that is why the state has tried to get this evidence into court “

Ruth “I think people in the UK people have been very surprised, there is a question of motive whether that can be presented in court case or just proving whatever the motive was whether I think that is something that people with little understanding of the SA legal system struggle to understand”

Script: Unlike in the Oscar trial, cameras have been kept strictly out the court room. Illustrator Pete Woodbridge has been hired to capture the atmosphere the traditional way.

Pete " I am not listening too much I am watching more, so that’s the part I actually like, it’s the voyeurism, I really like watching how people express themselves

John “What is your approach to drawing Shrien Dewani he’s not as emotional as Oscar Pistorious for example”

Pete " The challenge with Dewani is that he is so low down in the box his head is often down and he is looking at stuff so I don’t get a long time to look at him, the times that I do it’s a mutual stare out,

Script: Taxi Driver Zola Tongo was next in the stand, arguably the state’s most important witness. Tongo made a full confession over his role in the murder of Anni Dewani in 2010. He entered into a plea bargain with the state and was sentenced to 18 years imprisonment. It was Tongo’s confession that fingered Shrien Dewani as the one who ordered the hit on his wife. Photographer Fanie Jason covered Tongo’s sentencing

John "Tell us a bit more about Zola Tongo

Fanie "They were not your ordinary township type of person they looked very well off, well off in terms of township

Script: Zola Tongo grew up in Mfuleni Village on the Cape Flats and matriculated at Malibu High, going onto have a successful career as a tour guide and taxi driver. The two hitmen Qwabe and Mngeni on the other hand grew up in desperate circumstances

Fanie " The place where Qwabe lives is a very hard core area that is why it is very easy to find killers in that part of the world . Xholie was in a more desperate and pressing situation and he really needed the money. It very sad that people would have somebody murdered for 15000 but it is not just in the township that you wont be able to find people who would murder for less where than that

Script: But what’s surprised people, is that Zola Tongo had actually made something of his life chauffeuring wealthy clients like the Dewani’s

John “Tongo's behaviour on the Saturday afternoon of the killing was a little peculiar to say the least, he visited his mom, he visited his girlfriend, he even tried to call his pastor, I imaging that your readers back in the UK would find that surprising

Ruth "Somebody who has just agreed apparently to arrange the murder of somebody for the first time ever you know he says well I agreed to do it because Mr Dewani agreed to send all kinds of business my way in future. That somebody could decide to help murder someone on such flimsy promises is really shocking

Script: Tongo says he had a crisis of conscience just before he left to collect the Dewani’s on that fateful night, and tried to avert the murder,

Quote My knees were shaking and I was scared

Script : He called his taxi driver friend Da Vucks

Tongo Quote “I knew if Da Vucks goes there, what is supposed to happen, is not going to happen.

Script: But Da Vuks was not available so Tongo went ahead with the plan.

Tongo’s account of the events was told in complex Xhosa often using metaphorical language which the translator struggled to convey. He never used the word kill for example

Quote “ The job that he is having for me, there is somebody that he wants to be taken away from the eyes,.

Script: But despite speaking excellent English, he insisted on his right to a translator

Fanie "If you come from inside Cape Town, in the cities your Xhosa is different… his Xhosa is very deep Xhosa so the interpreter she has got a lot of problems

John “So possibly the Defence and Tongo aren’t on the same page because of the translation issues “

Fanie "Firstly you have got a Judge that don’t hear Xhosa you have got Adv Van Zyl who don’t hear Xhosa and you have got an interpreter that doesn’t interpret Xhosa properly so this case can actually get lost in translation

Link “ Zola Tongo’s lengthy evidence in chief continued on day 11 the state clarified that Tonga believed that the woman who got into the car on the Saturday night of the hijacking was Shrien Dewani’s business partner “

Ruth “The way he explained that was she looked very glamorous and I didn’t recognise her, and he has really stuck to that and sometimes it’s a bit unclear why he is so insistent this woman was the business partner but by saying it was the business partner rather than it was the wife it kind of sets him back slightly from the whole murder

Script "The State went on to show CCVTV footage from the Cape Grace where the Dewani’s were staying as well as the restaurant in Strand on the night of the hijacking. It was a remarkable revelation despite there being no sound on the video.

John “ Tongo spoke in his evidence how Shrien back at the hotel after the hijacking has approached him from time to time to find out what the latest was if he had any news if the killing had taken place, we have been show CCTV footage of that interaction do you think that was strange in any way?

Ruth "Well I do think that it does seem odd that Mr Dewani was hanging around in the hotel lobby so of sitting with a taxi driver that he had met a only a short while ago and also saw him ask the window cleaner to leave so he could talk in private with Mr Tongo what were they talking about what did they need to talk about in private

John “Considering that the CCTV Footage is silent can the judge draw her own conclusions?

William “The court might have to draw inferences, the law says if it is the only inferences that can be drawn from the facts and looking at the circumstances and if there are other inferences you can’t just say well that discussion had to be about a plan to commit a crime

Ruth "It takes more than CCVTV footage, silent CCTV footage where you can’t make out what people are saying it really does

William "So that is the test the state has to present sufficient evidence to prove beyond reasonable doubt that Dewani was involved in this plan to kill his wife

Link Zola Tongo is widely regarded as the states key witness not surprising then on day 12 Defence Adv Francois Van Zyl continues going through his evidence with a fine tooth comb

William "It is very difficult going to give evidence most people would rather now after they have watched the Oscar case,but people do make mistakes in their statements and that is why it is so important that police take down statements properly and that witnesses are properly prepared before they go give evidence

Script: Tongo repeatedly said that the inconsistencies in his evidence are because the police took down his statement incorrectly

Fanie "The nuances the words are missing it can be sometimes when you translate Xhosa words into English they never mean the same thing

Ruth "I think he has been quite pugnacious he has stood up to Francois Van Zyl……, he has stuck to his story and he defended the fact all the mistakes that Mr van Zyl has pointed out he has just said Oh well everyone makes mistakes

Final Link "So at the end of week 4 Zolo Tongo admits to various inconsistencies in his evidence as well as statements that he gave to the police after his arrest but he is sticking to his version that Shrien Dewani was going to pay him to have somebody killed
